_comment: DSH multi-window launcher configuration. ONE server, MANY windows is the default because each server process eagerly starts its own five stdio MCP bridges (~1.4 GB per server measured 2026-09-11). Set mode to 'multi' only when you deliberately want a second isolated engine.

_modes.single: One DSH server on primaryPort; every window attaches to it. Sessions are independent; the engine is shared. THIS IS THE ONLY SUPPORTED MODE.
_modes.multi: UNSUPPORTED on a shared DSH_HOME - do not use. Two dsh web processes on one home have been observed writing duplicate sequence numbers into one session log and making the whole history unloadable (see docs/multi-window/research-dsh-perf-config.md section 6). It is also ~1.4 GB per engine against ~3 GB total for one engine with twelve windows.

_fields.window.label: Human label, shown in the window title and in status output.
_fields.window.workspace: Default working directory (the agent's workspace root) opened in that window's sessions.
_fields.window.profile: Browser profile directory suffix. Must be unique per window: it is what gives each window its own cookie jar and its own 'last session'.
_fields.window.enabled: false keeps the slot defined but never opens it.
_fields.window.port: Only used in 'multi' mode: the port that window's own server listens on.

_memory._comment: profileMode decides how many browser PROCESS TREES exist. THE NUMBER OF WINDOWS IS UNCHANGED EITHER WAY - what changes is how much of a browser is duplicated per window.
_memory.per-window: LEGACY. Each window gets its own --user-data-dir, so its own cookie jar - and its own browser, GPU, crashpad, network and utility processes. Measured 2026-09-18 on ZABZ-YOGA: 7 windows on 7 private profiles cost 9 processes and 692-1064 MB each, mean ~892 MB, 6804 MB total for 74 msedge processes.
_memory.shared: One --user-data-dir for every window, so ONE browser process tree. Per-window session isolation is preserved by giving each window its own loopback ORIGIN instead (see the `origins` block): localStorage['dsh.sessions.current'] is keyed by origin, so a distinct port is a distinct session slot. Measured 2026-09-18: the shared tree costs its ~9 browser processes ONCE and each extra window adds roughly one renderer.

origins._comment: One loopback port alias per window slot, served by dshw-proxy.mjs, splicing to the single engine. Required by browser.profileMode='shared': without distinct origins every window would share ONE localStorage['dsh.sessions.current'] and last-writer-wins on reload. The same proxy also caches POST /api/session/list, which measured 25-31 s cold and 29 ms warm.
origins._basePortWhy: 2026-10-02: moved 3200 -> 3300. The block 3200..3223 included port 3216, which is the port the EA App's in-game-overlay IPC server binds. Our proxy held it permanently, so the EA App showed 'Communication error / couldn't connect to port 3216 / EC:10701' and warned it might block game launches. Measured: the proxy held 127.0.0.1:3200-3223 with `Get-NetTCPConnection`, and EA's own log recorded `IGOIPCClient ... Origin not found IGOIPC Server3216` from 2026-10-01 onward. Do NOT renumber this back into the low 3200s; EA's IPC also uses 5249 and 7544.

_geometry._comment: Default layout: a 4x2 grid on the primary 1440x900 display (work area 1440x852), read 2026-09-11. The machine also has three 2560x1440 panels (DISPLAY2/3/4). Per-window size/position here override browser.windowSize and are re-supplied on every launch, because Edge ignores them if an instance is already running.

_multiPorts._comment: Only read in mode 'multi'. Ports are assigned from basePort upward, in window order.

_dshInstall_note: FROZEN ENGINE PIN (2026-09-30). The npx cache is not a pin: a stray `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` re-resolved the floating range and changed the running engine, which is how ZABZ-YOGA broke. This path holds an exact version (0.2.0-rc.2) that nothing upgrades by accident; Resolve-DshBin probes it first.
